about.title: About World Zero
about.intro1: World Zero is a game you play in real life.
about.intro2: You play by going and doing cool things, telling us about it, and getting voted on by the comminty
about.step2: Actually do the task. Preferably in a really coll way
about.step3: To show us you did the task, write about it! Take pictures!
about.inspiredBody: World Zero is inspired by <1>SF0</1>, the original collaborative art game created in San Francisco. SF0 challenged players to complete tasks that blurred the line between game and life. World Zero carries that spirit forward as an open community platform.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.p1: The creator of the system of websites, events, and activities explicitly referred to as World Zero (henceforth, "Game"), assumes no responsibility for the actions of users (henceforth, "Players") of this website or any affiliated website (including but not limited to worldzero.org). This includes, but is not limited to, content posted to the Game by Players, suggested activities ("Tasks"), and actions taken by Players in particular or in general.
disclaimer.p2: As a Player, you agree to assume complete responsibility for any and all actions you or your character undertakes relating to you or your character's participation in the Game. You agree to submit no material to the Game that you have not created, or do not have permission to display publicly or reproduce in accordance with any applicable copyright. You agree that any action taken as part of your participation in the Game is in accordance with applicable laws and statutes - no violation of such is sanctioned by the Game. Any suggestion of any such violation that appears as part of the Game is due solely to the fictional nature of a game, and is not intended to condone or indemnify any violation of any local, state, or federal laws, nor any intrusion upon or violation of the rights of any Player, person, or persons.
disclaimer.p3: Due to the malleability of digital media, any appearance of such a violation by any Player may not be considered evidence, precedent, or approval of such a violation. Any material displayed as part of the Game should be considered fictive until and unless proven otherwise.
disclaimer.p4: If you delete your account, we keep a record for each service you signed in with: the name of the service plus a scrambled (salted hash) form of your ID there. It lets us recognize you if you come back, so we can show the "You deleted your World Zero account" screen. The record is cleared when you come back and start again; until then we keep it. Your account and characters are blanked, not erased: your praxis posts show as [removed], your comments are hidden, and your votes still count. Text you wrote into other players' collaborative praxis posts stays.

ai.title: AI at World Zero
ai.built:
Pixie here. Yes, this game was built using AI. For some that is a deal breaker and I get it (miss you Scout). After all, this game is about making art, and we very much discourage the use of AI when completing a praxis. Why did I build it this way

1) I tried building it the other way, and have paid over 5K to different people over 4 attempts to build it. For many reasons, this didn't end up working. 
2) AI took the primary activity of building this (namely writing code) from a slog to really really fun. Debugging doesn't put me into a whimsical place, but the use of AI took this from feeling like a logic problem to feeling like a creative project. For many disciplines, AI is seen as a replacement for the creative process, but for me, this really kick started it. 
3) While AI code can be questionable in quality, this is still much better, robust and more complete than if I had coded it myself. While I'm not a bad coder, this game is complex and ambitious across a variety of different technical disciplines.  
4) I could be more ambitious. There is no way I would have 7 design languages for 7 factions which went though countless passes without help.

Especially for assets like animations, I would prefer a human artist to come in and make something awesome. There is a contact page and I read those messages. But at time of writing, this is what I could afford/do. This game is 100% add free and we don't sell data, meaning our budget for hiring awesome professional artists and designers is somewhat limited. See AI involvement as an invitation for human improvement to the site, not as a devaluing of human involvement. There is no human contribution which was turned down in favor of an AI's version.

I am always open to feedback about how to make this place a place artists feel inspired and safe
ai.praxisTitle: Can I use AI in a Praxis?
ai.praxis:
For the most part no. In the same way finding out that the best man hired someone to write the wedding toast makes the words go hollow, so to would an AI writing praxis kind misunderstand the assignment. The point of a praxis is for you to reflect and articulate the journey you've taken in completing a task. Asking an AI to do that for you denies both you the reflection, and the reader from getting to know you. You may be a bad writer and self-conscious about this. I too am a bad writer and unfortunately, you get good at it by practicing. Same goes for images and video. The point of those is to show what you did. If you create a fake image of a cool stick, that is not the same experience as going and finding the cool stick.

There are acceptable use-cases for AI. Translation is one. This site (for now) is primarily English speaking. If you want to make praxis and don't speak English but engage with the English speaking community, that sounds awesome. As opposed to getting in the way of art in connection, AI in this case would facilitate it. I'm also open to use of AI for help with anonymizing a photo or video. You may want to play, but not as yourself and I think there are genuine use-cases where AI can enhance the creative process, not just take from it (such as the creation of this site.)

As a rule of thumb, if your praxis consists of "I asked AI to make an image or send and email" or something like that, I will probably flag it as slop and remove it. If you use AI as part of a larger effort like organizing contacts for starting a union, or coding something which does some kind of social good, I'll probably allow it. But things like that are the exception, not the rule.

attributions.title: Attributions
attributions.intro:
World Zero was built by many awesome people. I'm going to thank them now

Pixie - Fearless leader, Product/Builder, Game design. Also the person writing this copy :D 

Ty Odin - Game design. 

It took me 10 years, but I've brought your ideas to life. Thank you for the time and energy you gave both me, and this awesome creation you helped make. You were a fantastic inspiration to me both in the SF0 days and now. I'm looking forward to beating you at this version too.

Andrew - Everymen and Design

Thank you for being my husband, supporting me logistically, emotionally and financially while I worked away at this. Thank you also for the Everymen, they are a rad faction and I can't wait to see what people do with them.

Eli - Database consulting, Nitpicking, most of the good copy on the site, Ephemerists.

You are my creative rival/muse. Your writing contributions are what has taken this site from slop to superb (though we still have more to do). If there is something clever someone sees on the site, it was probably you.  I'm looking forward to immediately be-foeing you so when I see a taunt from you, I get busy

Robin - Unwavering Artists, Bugs

We walked 25 miles together for an SF0 task which took our friendship from classmates to people who still hang out 15 years later. I'm so excited to play this game with you. UA teaches us that imperfect art can still be good. Without your guidance, I would build this forever and never be able to set it free. 

Zylena - SNIDE, Singularity

You are the coolest person I know, and this game is to help other people have the go get em attitude that you do. I appreciate your time and creative energy helping to make something to inspire others, including me, have motivation to do the things you would just do on a Tuseday night. 

Joe and Ana - Nit Picks

Thank you both for helping spare the world from my spelling and some of my more... eccentric design choices. Both of you were deeply helpful and I hope you both enjoy playing what you helped build. 

I also want to credit SSI (Sean, Sam and Ian), the creators of SF0, the direct inspiration for this game.
They made a game that changed my life. It taught me that yes, I can just go out and do things that I feel need to be done. 
And their game needed new life breathed in. I hope they play, and I hope they enjoy 

Aside from these people, we also have to thank all of the AMAZING authors of open source tools which made this possible.

cookies.lead: We keep track of the bare minimum necessary to provide you a functional site. If you would like, you are welcome to send us a postcard with your personal details. Feel free to tell us about that new watch you bought. We'll send you back an advertisement for the same watch. That's what people use cookies for, right? We're not really sure.

essential.title: Essential — required
essential.help: One sign-in cookie, plus the choices your browser remembers for you.
essential.note: Some tracking is required for the site to work, unfortunately. If you prefer for the site not to work, you can throw your phone/computer in a volcano, but we don't recommend this. We do not track whether or not your phone is a pile of ash.
essential.switchName: Essential storage — always on, because the site cannot sign you in without it

analytics.help: Counts of who visits and which pages get used.
analytics.note: How many people visit this site? Who knows? Somewhere between 1 and 8,000,000, probably. We can still pay our server bills, so probably closer to that first one.

entries.titleSeen: A mark that this browser has seen the welcome title, so a later visit shows it at once instead of playing it again.

entries.pushAskDismissed: A mark that you closed the card offering notifications under your first praxis, so it is never shown again.

deletion.title: If you delete your account
deletion.body: Your praxis photos are removed. Your saved composer drafts are emptied. Your name, email, words and pictures are blanked. The votes you cast stay where they are, so nobody else's score moves.
deletion.hash: One thing is kept: which provider you signed in with, and a one-way hash of the ID that provider gave us. The hash cannot be turned back into the ID. It exists so that if you come back, we can tell you what happened to your old account.

language.lead: English is the only interface language today. Player-written content stays in the language it was written in.
language.requestHelp: Sumerian? Igpay Atinlay? A language people actually speak, like Spanish? Request away.
language.requestSent: Thanks — we'll let you know if enough players ask for the same one.
language.requestError: That did not send. Try again in a moment.

blocked.lead: Blocked players can't taunt you, and you won't see them in your friends-and-foes feed. They aren't told.
blocked.empty: You haven't blocked anyone. Block someone from their profile and they'll be listed here.
blocked.loadFailed: Could not load your block list. Try again later.

data.lead: Download everything tied to your account: your characters, the praxis you posted, the votes you cast, your comments, and the files you uploaded.
